explanation: Natural disasters kill people and destroy houses and property.

question: 53(b)(ii) State another effect of the natural changes named in (a) above.
subject: Science
answer: Famine and homelessness (any one: outbreak of diseases).
explanation: After floods or drought, people lack food and shelter and diseases may break out.

question: 54(a) Study the diagrams of houses below. Name the type of house shown in diagram M.
subject: Science
explanation: House M is built with strong lasting materials, so it is a permanent house.

question: 54(b)(i) Mention one material used to construct house N.
subject: Science
answer: Grass (any one: mud, poles, banana fibres).
explanation: House N is a temporary house built from local materials like grass and mud.

question: 54(b)(ii) Mention another material used to construct house N.
subject: Science
explanation: Mud walls are common in temporary houses.

question: 54(c) Give any one advantage of house M over house N.
subject: Science
answer: It is durable / lasts longer (any one: it resists bad weather, it is easy to keep clean).
explanation: A permanent house stands for many years while a temporary one needs frequent repair.

question: 55(a) Name any one exotic breed of rabbits kept in Uganda.
subject: Science
answer: California white (any one: New Zealand white, Angora).
explanation: California white is an exotic rabbit breed kept in Uganda for meat.

question: 55(b) Write down any one habit of rabbits you know.
subject: Science
answer: They burrow (any one: they feed on grass and vegetables).
explanation: Rabbits dig burrows in the ground where they live.

question: 55(c) Give any one rabbit disease that can attack poultry.
subject: Science
explanation: Coccidiosis attacks both rabbits and poultry, causing bloody diarrhoea.
hint: A disease of both rabbits and birds.

question: 55(d) State any one way in which rabbit farmers can keep their livestock healthy.
subject: Science
answer: Cleaning their hutches regularly (any one: proper feeding, vaccinating).
explanation: Clean hutches keep away germs that make rabbits sick.

question: 1. State one sign of pest attack on a crop.
subject: Science
answer: Holes in leaves (any one: wilting, yellow spots, stunted growth).
explanation: Pests chew parts of the crop, leaving holes in the leaves.

question: 2. In which state of matter does sound move fastest?
subject: Science
explanation: Sound travels fastest through solids because their particles are closely packed.

question: 3. Name the type of chicken kept for production of meat.
subject: Science
explanation: Broilers are chickens specially kept for meat production.

question: 4. What role does the fuse play in an electric circuit?
subject: Science
answer: It protects appliances by breaking the circuit when too much current flows.
explanation: The fuse wire melts when current is too high, stopping the flow and saving appliances.
hint: It breaks the circuit when current is too much.

question: 5. State one way transpiration benefits a plant.
subject: Science
answer: It cools the plant (any one: it helps in the absorption of water and mineral salts).
explanation: As water evaporates from leaves, the plant cools down and more water is pulled up from the roots.

question: 6. The diagram below shows a property of magnets. State the property of magnets shown above.
subject: Science
answer: Like poles repel each other while unlike poles attract each other.
explanation: When two magnets face each other, same poles push apart and different poles pull together.

question: 7. Give one activity done at school to promote sanitation.
subject: Science
answer: Sweeping the compound (any one: slashing, general cleaning, health parades).
explanation: Regular cleaning activities like sweeping keep the school free from germs.

question: 8. State one way a cobweb is important to a spider.
subject: Science
explanation: The spider's web catches flying insects which the spider eats.

question: 9. In which way can man make good use of wax got from bees?
subject: Science
explanation: Beeswax is used to make candles and shoe polish.

question: 10. Why do many crop farmers prefer growing annual crops to perennial crops?
subject: Science
answer: They mature and are harvested in a short time.
explanation: Annual crops complete their life in one season, giving farmers a quick harvest.

question: 11. How are valves important in the heart?
subject: Science
answer: They prevent the backflow of blood.
explanation: Valves in the heart allow blood to flow in one direction only.

question: 12. Name the immunisable disease that causes stiffness of muscles.
subject: Science
explanation: Tetanus makes the muscles, especially of the jaw, become stiff.

question: 13. Why is evening the best time for transplanting seedlings?
subject: Science
answer: It is cool, so seedlings lose less water and establish well overnight.
explanation: Evening coolness reduces wilting and gives seedlings the night to recover.

question: 14. Why is it not necessary to smoke a VIP latrine?
subject: Science
answer: The vent pipe removes the bad smell.
explanation: A VIP latrine has a vent that carries away smells, so smoking is not needed.

question: 15. How is the windsock at an airport important to a pilot?
subject: Science
answer: It shows the direction (and strength) of wind.
explanation: Pilots look at the windsock to know which way the wind blows before landing or taking off.

question: 16. Give a reason why the salivary amylase cannot continue digesting cooked starch even in the stomach.
subject: Science
answer: The acidic conditions in the stomach destroy it.
explanation: Salivary amylase works in the mouth, but stomach acid kills it so it stops working.

question: 17. State one way we can care for AIDS victims in our homes.
subject: Science
answer: Feeding them well on a balanced diet (any one: showing them love and care, counselling them).
explanation: AIDS victims need good nutrition, love and medical care to live longer.

question: 18. The diagram below shows a movable joint. Name the type of movable joint shown above.
subject: Science
explanation: The diagram shows a joint that moves in one direction like a door hinge, for example the knee.

question: 19. State one way part marked P is important at a joint.
subject: Science
answer: It reduces friction between the bones (it allows smooth movement).
explanation: Part P (cartilage/synovial fluid) cushions the bones so they move smoothly without rubbing.

question: 20. Apart from destroying crops, give any other effect of too much rain in the environment.
subject: Science
answer: It causes floods (any one: it causes soil erosion, it causes leaching).
explanation: Too much rain fills rivers and low areas, causing floods that destroy property.

question: 21. State one way diarrhoeal diseases can be controlled in our communities.
subject: Science
answer: Drinking boiled water (any one: proper use of latrines, washing hands).
explanation: Boiling water kills the germs that cause diarrhoeal diseases.

question: 22. Give one effect of alcoholism to the community.
subject: Science
answer: It leads to violence and poverty (any one: accidents, broken families).
explanation: Alcoholism causes fights, poverty and accidents in the community.

question: 23. When making charcoal, why is the piled wood covered with soil?
subject: Science
answer: To limit air (oxygen) so that the wood does not burn completely into ash.
explanation: With little air, the wood chars slowly into charcoal instead of burning into ashes.

question: 24. Why is it necessary to feed a malaria patient with green leafy vegetables?
subject: Science
answer: They are rich in iron, which helps to replace the blood destroyed by malaria.
explanation: Malaria destroys red blood cells, and iron from green vegetables helps the body make new blood.

question: 25. How does bush burning cause soil erosion?
subject: Science
answer: It destroys plant cover, leaving the soil bare and exposed to wind and running water.
explanation: Without plants to hold it, bare soil is easily carried away by wind and rain.

question: 26. Write down one characteristic of animal dispersed seeds.
subject: Science
answer: They have hooks that stick on animals (any one: they are fleshy and attractive, they have a sweet smell).
explanation: Some seeds have hooks that cling to animal fur so they are carried far.

question: 27. Draw a converging beam in the space below.
subject: Science
answer: Light rays drawn as straight lines meeting at one point (the focus).
explanation: A converging beam is a set of light rays that come together and meet at a point.

question: 28. State one reason why distilled water is not suitable for drinking.
subject: Science
answer: It lacks mineral salts needed by the body.
explanation: Distilled water has no dissolved minerals, so it does not supply the body's needs.

question: 29. Mention any one cause of improper growth of teeth.
subject: Science
answer: Lack of calcium in the diet (any one: poor feeding).
explanation: Teeth need calcium to grow strong; without it they grow poorly.

question: 30. Give a reason why water is added to the pit when making compost manure.
subject: Science
answer: To help the materials decompose (rot) faster.
explanation: Moisture helps the organisms that break down the materials to work quickly.

question: 31. The diagram below shows an iron box. Why is part marked T made out of wood?
subject: Science
answer: Wood is a poor conductor of heat, so the handle stays cool.
explanation: The handle of a charcoal iron is made of wood because wood does not conduct heat to the hand.

question: 32. How is the use of holes marked P different from that of holes marked W?
subject: Science
answer: Holes P let in fresh air to keep the charcoal burning, while holes W let out smoke.
explanation: Air enters through P to feed the fire, and smoke escapes through W.

question: 33. Give the main reason why farmers pollard fruit trees.
subject: Science
answer: To encourage the growth of many branches (for firewood and easy harvesting).
explanation: Cutting back the top makes the tree grow many new branches.

question: 34. Why is the use of biogas taken to be environmental friendly?
subject: Science
answer: It does not pollute the environment (it burns cleanly).
explanation: Biogas burns with a clean flame and uses animal waste, so it keeps the environment clean.

question: 35. Give one way living things depend on non-living things.
subject: Science
answer: Plants need water, air and sunlight to make food.
explanation: Living things need non-living things like water, air and sunlight to survive.

question: 36. Apart from dry lips, state any one other sign of dehydration in children.
subject: Science
answer: Sunken eyes (any one: dry skin, passing little urine).
explanation: A dehydrated child has sunken eyes and dry skin.

question: 37. Why is dew formed at night?
subject: Science
answer: The air cools at night and water vapour condenses into droplets.
explanation: At night temperatures fall, so water vapour in the air turns into tiny dew drops on cool surfaces.

question: 38. State one problem faced by people who rear goats.
subject: Science
answer: Diseases and parasites (any one: theft, predators).
explanation: Goats suffer from diseases and worms, and they may be stolen.

question: 39. What role does oxygen play during respiration?
subject: Science
answer: It helps to break down food to release energy.
explanation: Oxygen burns digested food in the body cells, releasing energy.

question: 40. Give one reason why some mothers bottle feed their babies instead of breast feeding.
subject: Science
answer: The mother may not produce enough milk (any one: the mother is sick or away at work).
explanation: Some mothers cannot breastfeed because of illness, work or low milk, so they use bottles.

question: 41(a)(i) State one sign of heat period in cattle.
subject: Science
answer: Mounting other cattle (any one: restlessness, bellowing, mucus discharge, loss of appetite).
explanation: A cow on heat mounts others and becomes restless, showing she is ready for mating.

question: 41(a)(ii) State another sign of heat period in cattle.
subject: Science
explanation: Cows on heat move about restlessly and moo loudly.

question: 41(b) What advice would you give to a farmer whose cow is on heat?
subject: Science
answer: Take the cow for mating (or call a veterinary doctor for artificial insemination).
explanation: A cow on heat should be served by a bull or inseminated so that she can conceive.

question: 41(c) Give one reason why cattle keepers are advised to graze cows and bulls separately.
subject: Science
answer: To control breeding (to prevent unwanted mating).
explanation: Keeping bulls away from cows stops unplanned pregnancies and inbreeding.

question: 42(a)(i) Write down one condition necessary for photosynthesis to take place.
subject: Science
answer: Sunlight (any one: chlorophyll, carbon dioxide, water).
explanation: Plants need sunlight energy to make food during photosynthesis.

question: 42(a)(ii) Write down another condition necessary for photosynthesis to take place.
subject: Science
explanation: Chlorophyll traps sunlight for the plant to use in making food.

question: 42(b) Why can't photosynthesis take place at night?
subject: Science
answer: There is no sunlight at night.
explanation: Photosynthesis needs light energy, which is absent at night.

question: 42(c) In which way does photosynthesis benefit the environment?
subject: Science
answer: It releases oxygen and absorbs carbon dioxide, purifying the air.
explanation: Plants clean the air by taking in carbon dioxide and giving out oxygen.

question: 43(a) The diagram below shows a kidney. Name part marked T.
subject: Science
explanation: Part T is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder, called the ureter.

question: 43(b) How is part marked X important in the kidney?
subject: Science
answer: It carries blood into the kidney for filtration.
explanation: Part X (the renal artery) brings blood with waste products into the kidney to be cleaned.

question: 43(c) State one substance that gets reabsorbed into the body in part marked Y.
subject: Science
explanation: As urine flows through the tubules, useful substances like water and glucose are taken back into the blood.

question: 43(d) Apart from excretion mention any other use of the kidney in the body.
subject: Science
answer: It regulates the amount of water and salts in the body (osmoregulation).
explanation: Besides removing waste, the kidney balances water and salts in the body.

question: 44(a) Give one reason why many poultry farmers in Uganda today prefer keeping exotic breeds of poultry.
subject: Science
answer: They grow fast and lay many eggs.
explanation: Exotic birds mature quickly and are more productive than local birds.

question: 44(b) State one problem faced by poultry farmers in Uganda.
subject: Science
answer: Outbreak of diseases (any one: expensive feeds, lack of market).
explanation: Diseases can kill many birds and cause big losses to poultry farmers.

question: 44(c) Name the poultry disease that can be identified by blood stained diarrhoea and ruffled feathers.
subject: Science
explanation: Coccidiosis in poultry shows bloody diarrhoea and ruffled feathers.

question: 44(d) Mention one way poultry diseases can be controlled.
subject: Science
answer: Vaccinating the birds (any one: proper hygiene, isolating sick birds).
explanation: Vaccination protects birds against killer poultry diseases.

question: 45(a)(i) State one way food can get contaminated.
subject: Science
answer: Leaving food uncovered (any one: handling food with dirty hands, using dirty utensils).
explanation: Uncovered food collects germs from flies and dust.

question: 45(a)(ii) State another way food can get contaminated.
subject: Science
explanation: Dirty hands pass germs directly to food.

question: 45(b) Mention one disease a person can get if he eats contaminated food.
subject: Science
explanation: Contaminated food carries germs that cause cholera, typhoid and dysentery.

question: 45(c) Give one reason why we need to cover food when cooking it.
subject: Science
answer: To prevent it from getting contaminated (and to cook faster).
explanation: Covering food keeps dirt out and keeps heat in so it cooks quickly.

question: 46(a) The diagram below shows a doctor's prescription. How many tablets should the patient take in a day?
subject: Science
answer: 6 tablets (2 tablets three times a day).
explanation: The prescription directs the patient to take 2 tablets three times daily, which is 6 tablets a day.

question: 46(b) Write down any one condition under which drugs should be stored.
subject: Science
answer: In a cool, dry place (any one: away from children).
explanation: Drugs kept in a cool dry place away from children remain safe and effective.

question: 46(c) Give one reason why drugs should be labeled.
subject: Science
answer: To show how they should be used (dosage) and their expiry date.
explanation: Labels tell the patient the correct dose and when the drug expires.

question: 46(d) Apart from age and weight, give any other factor medical workers consider before prescribing a drug.
subject: Science
answer: The type of sickness (any one: the patient's medical history, allergies).
explanation: The doctor must know the disease and the patient's history before choosing a drug.

question: 47(a)(i) Mention one cause of a short circuit in electricity.
subject: Science
answer: Naked wires touching each other (any one: overloading, faulty appliances).
explanation: When bare wires touch, current takes a shortcut, causing a short circuit.

question: 47(a)(ii) Mention another cause of a short circuit in electricity.
subject: Science
explanation: Too many appliances on one circuit can cause a short circuit.

question: 47(b) Write down one danger that can be brought by a short circuit.
subject: Science
answer: It can cause fire (any one: it destroys appliances, it causes electric shock).
explanation: Short circuits produce heat that can start fires and burn appliances.

question: 47(c) In which way do people who install electricity guard against electric shocks?
subject: Science
answer: By using insulated wires and proper earthing.
explanation: Insulation and earthing stop electricity from reaching people.

question: 48(a) Give the main reason why our bodies carry out respiration.
subject: Science
explanation: Respiration breaks down food in body cells to set free energy for work.

question: 48(b) Where does respiration take place in the body?
subject: Science
explanation: Food is broken down to release energy inside every living body cell.

question: 48(c) What role does oxygen play during respiration?
subject: Science
answer: It helps to break down food to release energy.
explanation: Oxygen burns digested food in the cells, setting energy free.

question: 48(d) How does respiration affect the environment negatively?
subject: Science
answer: It releases carbon dioxide into the air.
explanation: Breathing out adds carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas, to the atmosphere.

question: 49(a) What is thinning?
subject: Science
answer: The removal of excess seedlings from a nursery or garden bed.
explanation: Thinning means pulling out extra young plants so the rest have enough space.

question: 49(b)(i) Give one reason why farmers thin their crops.
subject: Science
answer: To reduce competition for nutrients, water and sunlight.
explanation: Thinning gives each plant enough space, food and light to grow well.

question: 49(b)(ii) Give another reason why farmers thin their crops.
subject: Science
answer: So that the remaining crops grow healthy and give a good harvest.
explanation: Well-spaced crops grow bigger and yield more.

question: 49(c) State one way farmers can make good use of thinned crops.
subject: Science
answer: They can be used as vegetables or animal feed (any one: they can be transplanted).
explanation: Thinned seedlings need not be wasted; they can feed animals or people.

question: 50(a) The diagram below shows an experiment carried out in a science lesson. Name container marked W.
subject: Science
explanation: Container W is a measuring cylinder used to measure the volume of water displaced by the stone.

question: 50(b) What was the experiment about?
subject: Science
answer: Finding the volume of a stone (an irregular object) by displacement.
explanation: The stone was lowered into water and the rise in water level showed its volume.

question: 50(c) Why did the teacher decide to use such a method?
subject: Science
answer: Because the stone has an irregular shape (it cannot be measured with a ruler).
explanation: Irregular objects have no simple length, width and height, so displacement is used.

question: 50(d) State the volume of the stone.
subject: Science
answer: The difference between the two water levels (final reading minus initial reading).
explanation: The volume of the stone equals the volume of water it displaces, read from the rise in level.

question: 51(a)(i) Give one reason why we need to keep our bodies clean.
subject: Science
explanation: A clean body keeps away germs that cause diseases.

question: 51(a)(ii) Give another reason why we need to keep our bodies clean.
subject: Science
answer: To remove bad smell (any one: to look smart).
explanation: Bathing removes sweat and dirt that cause bad body smell.

question: 51(b) How does the washing of clothes keep them clean?
subject: Science
answer: It removes dirt and germs from them.
explanation: Washing with soap and water takes dirt and germs out of clothes.

question: 51(c) Mention one place where cleaned clothes can be kept.
subject: Science
answer: In a wardrobe (any one: drawer, suitcase).
explanation: Clean clothes are kept in wardrobes or drawers to stay clean.

question: 52(a) The diagram below shows a type of pulley. Name the type of pulley.
subject: Science
explanation: The diagram shows a pulley fixed in one position, which changes the direction of effort.

question: 52(b) Through what distance did the effort move by the time the load reached point B?
subject: Science
answer: The same distance as the load moved (in a single fixed pulley, effort distance equals load distance).
explanation: With a fixed pulley, the rope moves equally on both sides, so effort and load cover the same distance.

question: 52(c) State one advantage of using such pulley.
subject: Science
answer: It changes the direction of effort, making work easier.
explanation: A fixed pulley lets one pull down to lift a load up, which is easier.

question: 52(d) Give one use of such a pulley in our daily life.
subject: Science
answer: Drawing water from a well (any one: raising a flag).
explanation: Fixed pulleys are used on wells to lift water and on flag poles.

question: 53(a) Why is a frog able to live in water?
subject: Science
answer: It breathes through its moist skin (any one: it has webbed feet for swimming).
explanation: A frog can absorb oxygen from water through its moist skin.

question: 53(b) Mention one way a frog is different from a toad.
subject: Science
answer: A frog has smooth, moist skin while a toad has rough, dry, warty skin.
explanation: Frogs live mostly in water but toads live mostly on land, and their skins differ.

question: 53(c) Write down one characteristic of amphibians.
subject: Science
answer: They live part of their life in water and part on land (any one: they lay their eggs in water).
explanation: Amphibians like frogs start life in water and later live on land.

question: 53(d) Toads spend most of their adult time on land. Why do they go in water?
subject: Science
explanation: Toads return to water to lay eggs, since their young develop in water.

question: 54(a) Mention one place in a home where near drowning can take place.
subject: Science
answer: In a well (any one: swimming pool, water tank).
explanation: Open wells and pools at home are places where children can drown.

question: 54(b) During first aid for near drowning, why is it necessary to press the chest hard?
subject: Science
answer: To force water out of the lungs (and help the victim to breathe).
explanation: Pressing the chest pushes swallowed water out so that air can enter the lungs.

question: 54(c) How can a young boy help a person who is near-drowning?
subject: Science
answer: By throwing them a rope or float (without jumping into the water).
explanation: A boy should extend a stick or throw something that floats, and call for help.

question: 54(d) State one way of preventing near-drowning at home.
subject: Science
answer: Covering open wells (any one: fencing the pool, supervising children near water).
explanation: Covered wells and fenced pools keep children from falling into water.

question: 55(a) How are the health parades important in a school?
subject: Science
answer: They help to check pupils' personal hygiene.
explanation: During health parades, teachers inspect cleanliness of pupils, encouraging good hygiene.

question: 55(b) Write down one role of a health prefect in a school.
subject: Science
answer: Ensures the school compound is clean (any one: organises cleaning).
explanation: The health prefect leads pupils in keeping the school clean.

question: 55(c) Apart from the sanitary prefect, mention any one other member of a school health committee.
subject: Science
answer: The headteacher (any one: class teacher, school nurse).
explanation: The school health committee includes teachers and the headteacher besides the sanitary prefect.

question: 55(d) Give one way we can care for the people with special needs in a community.
subject: Science
answer: By helping them with their needs (showing them love and care).
explanation: People with special needs should be assisted and treated with kindness.

question: 1. Why does a bedbug produce a very bad smell when it is touched?
subject: Science
answer: To scare away its enemies (for defence).
explanation: A bedbug releases a bad smell as a defence to frighten away animals that touch it.
hint: Think about how the smell protects the bedbug.

question: 2. Give any one way in which flowers are important to a plant.
subject: Science
answer: They help the plant to reproduce (they develop into seeds and fruits).
explanation: Flowers are the reproductive parts of a plant; after pollination they form seeds and fruits.
hint: What do flowers turn into after pollination?

question: 3. Which deficiency disease in children has these signs and symptoms: swollen moon face, brownish hair and pot belly?
subject: Science
explanation: Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins in the diet and shows a swollen face, brownish hair and a pot belly.
hint: It is caused by lack of proteins.

question: 4. Write one common characteristic which is common in all arachnids.
subject: Science
answer: They have four pairs of walking legs (eight legs).
explanation: All arachnids such as spiders, ticks and scorpions have eight legs and their bodies are divided into two parts.
hint: Count the legs of a spider.

question: 5. Why does sugar disappear when it is mixed in water?
subject: Science
explanation: When sugar is mixed with water it dissolves, forming a solution, so it seems to disappear.
hint: What happens to a solute in a solvent?

question: 6. Which property of air is demonstrated when air is pumped into a ball and it becomes bigger?
subject: Science
explanation: The ball becomes bigger because the air pumped into it takes up space inside the ball.
hint: The air fills up the inside of the ball.

question: 7. How is the absence of vitamin D harmful to our health?
subject: Science
explanation: Vitamin D helps the body to use calcium for strong bones; without it children develop rickets.
hint: Which bone disease comes from lack of vitamin D?

question: 8. What is the importance of blood platelets in the body?
subject: Science
answer: They help blood to clot (stop bleeding).
explanation: When you are cut, platelets gather at the wound and make the blood clot so that bleeding stops.
hint: What stops bleeding when you are cut?

question: 9. Give one reason why a farmer should keep records of daily weather.
subject: Science
answer: To plan farming activities (for example, to know when to plant crops).
explanation: Weather records help a farmer decide the best time for planting, weeding and harvesting.
hint: How do the records help in planning?

question: 10. Why is proper disposal of wastes important in a home?
subject: Science
answer: It prevents the spread of diseases.
explanation: Wastes left anyhow breed germs and vectors, so proper disposal keeps the home free from diseases.
hint: What do heaps of rubbish cause?

question: 11. Which of the following animals: fish, frog, lizard, rat and a snail is warm blooded?
subject: Science
explanation: A rat is a mammal, and mammals are warm blooded; the other animals are cold blooded.

question: 12. In the space provided below, draw a symbol of a switch.
subject: Science
answer: A switch symbol: a break in a straight wire with a short slanting line (lever) bridging the gap.
explanation: The switch symbol shows a wire with a small gap and a lever that can close the gap to complete the circuit.
hint: It looks like a wire with a little door that opens and closes.

question: 13. What type of energy is possessed by a stone resting on the table?
subject: Science
explanation: A stone resting above the ground has stored energy because of its position; this is potential energy.
hint: It is stored energy due to position.

question: 14. When water is heated it changes into steam. What is this process called?
subject: Science
explanation: Heating water changes it from liquid to gas (steam); this change of state is called evaporation.

question: 15. Name any one example of a perennial crop.
subject: Science
answer: Mango (any one: coffee, banana, avocado, orange).
explanation: Perennial crops live for many years; mango, coffee and banana are common examples.
hint: Name a crop that lives for many years.

question: 16. How does paddock system of grazing cattle control the spread of tick borne diseases?
subject: Science
answer: It breaks the life cycle of ticks (ticks starve and die while a paddock rests without cattle).
explanation: Moving cattle from paddock to paddock leaves ticks without animals to feed on, so the ticks die.
hint: What happens to ticks when no cattle are around?

question: 17. Give any one reason why we should wring clothes before drying them.
subject: Science
answer: To remove excess water so that the clothes dry faster.
explanation: Wringing squeezes out most of the water, leaving less water to evaporate in the sun.
hint: Less water left means faster drying.

question: 18. Write down any one part which makes the stamen on a flower.
subject: Science
explanation: The stamen is the male part of a flower and is made up of the anther and the filament.
hint: Name the male part's head or stalk.

question: 19. Give one reason why a farmer should practice thinning of his crops.
subject: Science
answer: To reduce competition for nutrients, water and sunlight so that the remaining crops grow well.
explanation: Crowded seedlings compete for food and light; thinning gives each plant enough space to grow healthy.
hint: What do crowded plants compete for?

question: 20. Vultures, kites and crows were found feeding on rotting meat. What group of birds are these?
subject: Science
explanation: Vultures, kites and crows feed on flesh, so they belong to the group called birds of prey.

question: 21. Give any one special characteristic of the air we breathe in.
subject: Science
answer: It contains a lot of oxygen.
explanation: The air we breathe in is rich in oxygen, which the body needs to release energy from food.
hint: Which gas is plenty in breathed-in air?

question: 22. What is the function of synovial fluid in the knee joint?
subject: Science
answer: It lubricates the joint (reduces friction between the bones).
explanation: Synovial fluid is like oil in the joint; it lets the bones move smoothly without rubbing.
hint: It works like oil in a machine.

question: 23. Give the main cause of fainting.
subject: Science
answer: Insufficient supply of blood (and oxygen) to the brain.
explanation: When the brain does not get enough blood and oxygen, a person faints.
hint: The brain lacks blood and oxygen.

question: 24. Mention one service provided under ante-natal care.
subject: Science
answer: Immunising mothers against tetanus (any one: examining the mother, giving health education).
explanation: During ante-natal care, mothers are examined, immunised and taught how to care for themselves and the baby.
hint: What do health workers do for pregnant mothers?

question: 25. Which blood vessel transports digested food from the ileum to the liver?
subject: Science
explanation: After absorption in the ileum, digested food is carried to the liver by the hepatic portal vein.
hint: It is a special vein going to the liver.

question: 26. The diagram below shows a chalk box (5 cm by 4 cm by 6 cm). Find its volume.
subject: Science
explanation: Volume = length x width x height = 6 cm x 5 cm x 4 cm = 120 cm3.

question: 27. Study the animals given in list K (FISH, BIRD, FROG) and those in list M (MAN, WHALE, BAT). How are animals in list K similar to those in list M?
subject: Science
answer: They are all vertebrates (they all have backbones).
explanation: Fish, birds, frogs, man, whales and bats all have backbones, so they are all vertebrates.
hint: What body structure do they all share?

question: 28. What is the source of energy in thermal electricity?
subject: Science
answer: Heat (from burning fuel such as coal, oil or peat).
explanation: Thermal electricity is generated using heat produced by burning fuels.

question: 29. Why is it a bad practice for people to share a house with domestic animals?
subject: Science
answer: Animals can spread diseases and parasites to people.
explanation: Domestic animals carry germs, ticks and fleas which can easily pass to people sharing the house.

question: 30. State the use of a stretcher when giving First Aid to a victim with a fracture.
subject: Science
answer: To carry the casualty safely without worsening the fracture.
explanation: A stretcher keeps the injured part still while the victim is carried, so the fracture does not get worse.
hint: It keeps the broken part still during carrying.

question: 31. How does a vent help to reduce smell in a VIP latrine?
subject: Science
answer: It lets out the bad smell (gases) from the pit.
explanation: The vent pipe carries smelly gases from the pit up into the air, away from the latrine users.

question: 32. Write down one danger of buying drugs from local shops or markets.
subject: Science
answer: The drugs may be expired or fake (any one: wrong drug, wrong dosage).
explanation: Drugs sold in markets may be expired, fake or wrongly measured, which can harm the patient.
hint: The drugs may not be genuine.

question: 33. Name one material used to guard against electric shock.
subject: Science
explanation: Insulators like rubber and plastic do not conduct electricity, so they protect people from electric shock.

question: 34. Draw prop roots in the space provided below.
subject: Science
answer: Prop roots grow out from the lower part of the stem and go down into the soil, supporting the plant (as in maize).
explanation: Prop roots are extra roots that grow from the stem above the ground to give the plant extra support.
hint: They grow from the stem into the soil to support the plant.

question: 35. Which body system is commonly affected by polio?
subject: Science
explanation: Polio attacks the nerves, which is why it can cause paralysis of the limbs.

question: 36. State one process by which soil is formed.
subject: Science
explanation: Soil is formed when rocks are broken down into small particles by weathering.
hint: Rocks are broken down by it.

question: 37. Give one use of an axe at home.
subject: Science
explanation: An axe is used at home mainly for splitting firewood into pieces.

question: 38. What happens to the blood as it passes through the kidneys?
subject: Science
answer: Waste products (urea, excess water and salts) are removed from it.
explanation: The kidneys filter the blood, removing waste materials which leave the body as urine.

question: 39. Study the diagram of a leaf below. What is part marked B?
subject: Science
explanation: Part B is the stalk that joins the leaf blade to the stem; it is called the petiole.
hint: It joins the leaf blade to the stem.

question: 40. Give one of the functions of the structures marked A on a leaf.
subject: Science
answer: They allow gaseous exchange (they let in carbon dioxide and release oxygen and water vapour).
explanation: The structures marked A are stomata, tiny openings through which gases move in and out of the leaf.
hint: They are tiny openings for gases.

question: 1. Mention any one example of a childhood immunisable disease.
subject: Science
answer: Polio (any one: measles, tuberculosis, diphtheria, tetanus).
explanation: Childhood immunisable diseases like polio and measles are prevented by vaccination.

question: 2. Identify the part of the digestive system where alcohol is absorbed.
subject: Science
explanation: Alcohol is absorbed mainly through the walls of the stomach into the blood.

question: 3. In which way does the use of solar energy for cooking help to conserve the environment?
subject: Science
answer: It reduces the cutting down of trees for firewood.
explanation: Cooking with the sun saves trees, keeping forests that protect the environment.

question: 4. How are screws similar to wheels and axles in the way they simplify work?
subject: Science
answer: Both are simple machines that make work easier.
explanation: Screws and wheels-and-axles are simple machines that help people do work with less effort.

question: 5. Name the type of germ which causes ringworm infection.
subject: Science
explanation: Ringworm is a skin infection caused by a fungus, not a worm.

question: 6. How is the cause of burns similar to that of scalds?
subject: Science
explanation: Burns come from dry heat like fire, and scalds from wet heat like steam, but both are heat injuries.

question: 7. Give one way in which reflection of light is useful to people.
subject: Science
answer: It enables us to see (any one: mirrors help us see behind, periscopes).
explanation: We see objects when light reflects off them into our eyes; mirrors use reflection too.

question: 8. What term refers to the practice of growing crops and trees together on the same piece of land?
subject: Science
explanation: Agroforestry is the growing of crops and trees together on the same land.

question: 9. In the diagram below, a plastic comb was rubbed against a woollen cloth and it was brought nearer to small pieces of paper. Why is the plastic comb able to attract the pieces of paper as shown above?
subject: Science
answer: The comb became electrically charged (static electricity).
explanation: Rubbing the comb charges it with static electricity, which then attracts the light paper pieces.

question: 10. What form of energy is stored in a candle?
subject: Science
explanation: A candle stores chemical energy in its wax, released as light and heat when it burns.

question: 11. Name the fungal-caused sexually transmitted disease which is spread through poor hygiene.
subject: Science
explanation: Candidiasis is a fungal infection spread through poor hygiene.

question: 12. Which method of heat transfer helps farmers to dry their harvested crops?
subject: Science
explanation: The sun's heat reaches crops by radiation and dries them.

question: 13. Give one sign of pest and disease attack on tuber crops.
subject: Science
answer: Holes in the leaves (any one: rotting tubers, wilting).
explanation: Pests chew leaves leaving holes, and diseases rot the tubers.

question: 14. Identify one condition needed by bacteria to multiply.
subject: Science
explanation: Bacteria multiply fast where it is warm and moist with food available.

question: 15. Give any one good effect of changes in the environment.
subject: Science
answer: Rain provides water for crops to grow.
explanation: Environmental changes like rainfall bring water needed by plants and animals.

question: 16. How can foot and mouth disease be controlled on a farm?
subject: Science
answer: Vaccinating the animals (any one: quarantine, restricting animal movement).
explanation: Vaccination and quarantine stop foot and mouth disease from spreading among animals.

question: 17. Study the diagram below and answer the questions about it. How are structures marked X useful to the above organism?
subject: Science
explanation: The structures marked X are wings, which let the organism fly from place to place.

question: 18. Which disease is spread by the above organism to people?
subject: Science
explanation: The organism (housefly) carries germs from faeces to food, spreading cholera and similar diseases.

question: 19. How is the above organism similar to a maggot?
subject: Science
answer: The maggot is the larval stage that grows into the organism (both are stages of the housefly's life cycle).
explanation: A maggot develops through pupa into the adult organism, the housefly.

question: 20. Why should a pig sty have a slanting floor?
subject: Science
answer: So that urine and washing water drain out easily.
explanation: A slanting floor lets waste water flow out, keeping the sty clean and dry.

question: 21. Give one way in which music stored by staff notation can be reproduced.
subject: Science
answer: By singing or playing it on instruments.
explanation: Written music in staff notation can be read and performed by singers and instrumentalists.

question: 22. In the space below, draw a vein and show the flow of blood in it.
subject: Science
answer: A blood vessel drawn with valves inside and an arrow showing blood flowing towards the heart.
explanation: Veins carry blood back to the heart and have valves that stop blood flowing backwards.

question: 23. Give one factor that leads to sickness in a home.
subject: Science
explanation: Dirty homes breed germs that make family members sick.

question: 24. What type of root system does an onion plant have?
subject: Science
explanation: Onions have many thin spreading roots, which form a fibrous root system.

question: 25. Apart from production of eggs (ova), mention one other use of the ovaries in the human body.
subject: Science
explanation: The ovaries also make hormones that bring about female body changes.

question: 26. How does a sweater help to keep a person warm during cold days?
subject: Science
answer: It traps warm air and prevents body heat from escaping.
explanation: A sweater holds a layer of warm air around the body, keeping heat in.

question: 27. Write down any one example of an animal fibre.
subject: Science
explanation: Wool from sheep is an animal fibre used to make clothes.

question: 28. State the compass direction in which a freely suspended magnet will rest.
subject: Science
explanation: A freely hanging magnet always settles pointing north and south.

question: 29. Give any one property of air in the diagram below.
subject: Science
explanation: The diagram shows that air takes up space inside a container.

question: 30. Which body sense is used by Phionah to know whether Alex has dressed perfume?
subject: Science
explanation: Perfume is detected by the nose, the organ of smell.

question: 31. Why is photosynthesis important to animals?
subject: Science
answer: It provides oxygen for breathing (and food for animals).
explanation: Animals depend on plants for the oxygen they breathe and the food they eat.

question: 32. What process makes dew to disappear during hot days?
subject: Science
explanation: Heat turns dew drops into water vapour, which is evaporation.

question: 33. What group of birds are vultures, kites and crows?
subject: Science
explanation: Vultures, kites and crows feed on flesh, so they are birds of prey.

question: 34. Why does an insect die when its abdomen is placed in oil for some time?
subject: Science
answer: Oil blocks its breathing holes (spiracles), so it suffocates.
explanation: Insects breathe through tiny holes on the abdomen; oil covers them and stops air entering.

question: 35. Give any one special characteristic of the air we breathe out.
subject: Science
answer: It contains a lot of carbon dioxide (any one: it is warm and moist).
explanation: Breathed-out air is rich in carbon dioxide produced in the body.

question: 36. Find the density of an object whose mass is 19 g and volume is 5 cm3.
subject: Science
explanation: Density = mass / volume = 19 g / 5 cm3 = 3.8 g/cm3.

question: 37. Why does smoke go up when firewood is burning?
subject: Science
answer: Smoke is hot and less dense than the surrounding air, so it rises.
explanation: Hot smoke is lighter than cool air, so it floats upward.

question: 38. Give one reason why drugs should be prescribed by health workers before they are used by sick people.
subject: Science
answer: To get the right drug and correct dosage (any one: to avoid misuse).
explanation: Health workers choose the correct medicine and amount for each sickness.

question: 39. What feature enables a housefly to spread diseases?
subject: Science
answer: Its hairy body and legs trap germs.
explanation: Germs stick to the housefly's hairy body and legs and are carried to food.

question: 40. Give any one characteristic of flowers which attract moths to visit them at night.
subject: Science
answer: They produce a sweet scent (any one: white petals visible at night).
explanation: Night flowers attract moths with strong sweet smells and pale petals.

question: 41(a) The diagram below shows a simple circuit. Study it carefully. Name the part marked with letter T.
subject: Science
explanation: Part T is the bulb, which lights when the circuit is complete.

question: 41(b) Give the function of the part marked with letter M.
subject: Science
answer: It provides electricity (it is the source of power in the circuit).
explanation: Part M is the dry cell (battery) which pushes electric current round the circuit.

question: 41(c) State any one energy change which takes place in an electric bulb when part labeled K is closed.
subject: Science
answer: Electrical energy changes to light and heat energy.
explanation: When the switch K is closed, current flows and the bulb turns electrical energy into light (and heat).

question: 41(d) Using an arrow, show the direction of the flow of electrons in the diagram above.
subject: Science
answer: Electrons flow from the negative terminal of the cell to the positive terminal round the circuit.
explanation: In a circuit, electrons move from the negative side of the battery, through the wires, to the positive side.

question: 42(a) State the difference between endoskeleton and exoskeleton.
subject: Science
answer: An endoskeleton is found inside the body while an exoskeleton is found outside the body.
explanation: People have skeletons inside their bodies (endoskeleton), while insects wear theirs outside (exoskeleton).

question: 42(b) State the protective function of the skull to the human skeleton.
subject: Science
explanation: The skull is a hard bony case that shields the delicate brain from injury.

question: 42(c)(i) Write one advantage of maintaining proper body posture.
subject: Science
answer: It prevents backache and deformity of the body.
explanation: Sitting and standing upright keeps the backbone in good shape.

question: 42(c)(ii) Write another advantage of maintaining proper body posture.
subject: Science
answer: It allows proper breathing and blood flow (any one: one looks smart).
explanation: Good posture lets the lungs and heart work well.

question: 43(a) Why do earthworms come out of the soil after it has rained?
subject: Science
answer: Their holes get filled with water, so they come out to breathe.
explanation: Earthworms breathe through moist skin and cannot breathe under water in flooded holes.

question: 43(b)(i) Give one way in which earthworms are useful to farmers.
subject: Science
answer: They aerate the soil (they make air spaces as they burrow).
explanation: Burrowing earthworms open up the soil so air and water enter easily.

question: 43(b)(ii) Give another way in which earthworms are useful to farmers.
subject: Science
answer: Their droppings add fertility to the soil.
explanation: Earthworm droppings are rich in nutrients that feed crops.

question: 43(c) To which group of animals do earthworms belong?
subject: Science
explanation: Earthworms have segmented bodies, so they belong to the annelids.

question: 44(a) The diagram below is an experiment performed by a P.7 class (copper rod with vaseline and clips, heated at one end). What is the experiment about?
subject: Science
answer: How heat travels through a metal (conduction).
explanation: The experiment shows heat moving along the copper rod from the hot end, melting vaseline at each clip.

question: 44(b) What is the importance of vaseline in the experiment?
subject: Science
answer: It holds the clips in place (it melts when heat reaches it).
explanation: Vaseline sticks the clips to the rod; when heat arrives, it melts and the clip falls.

question: 44(c) What will happen to vaseline in clip 4 after some time?
subject: Science
answer: It will melt and the clip will fall.
explanation: Heat travels along the rod to clip 4, melting its vaseline last.

question: 44(d) Give a reason for your answer.
subject: Science
answer: Heat travels from the hot end to the cold end of the rod by conduction.
explanation: Conduction carries heat along the metal until it reaches the last clip.

hint: They are also called deciduous teeth.

question: 55(b) How are molars and pre molars adapted to their function?
subject: Science
answer: They have broad flat tops for grinding and crushing food
explanation: Molars and premolars have wide flat ridged surfaces that crush food into small pieces.
hint: Their flat tops suit their grinding job.

question: 55(c) Give two teeth disorders apart from broken teeth. (i) ___
subject: Science
explanation: Germs acting on food remains on teeth cause decay and holes called cavities.
hint: Holes caused by germs on unbrushed teeth.

question: 55(c) Give two teeth disorders apart from broken teeth. (ii) ___
subject: Science
explanation: Poor cleaning of teeth makes the gums swell, sore and bleed.

question: Mention any one example of a wild bird.
subject: Science
explanation: Wild birds like the crested crane live freely in swamps and forests.

question: Which part of a fish has similar function as stomata on a plant?
subject: Science
explanation: Gills take in dissolved oxygen for the fish, just as stomata take in air for the plant.

question: Give the function of valves in the human heart.
subject: Science
answer: They prevent the backflow of blood
explanation: Valves open and close so that blood flows in one direction only.
hint: They stop blood from flowing backwards.

question: In which way is a smoker important to a person harvesting honey?
subject: Science
answer: It produces smoke that calms the bees
explanation: Smoke makes bees calm and less likely to sting during honey harvesting.

question: How is early sex dangerous to children at school?
subject: Science
answer: It leads to teenage pregnancy, HIV/AIDS infection and dropping out of school
explanation: Early sex exposes children to pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases, ending their schooling.
hint: It can end a child's education.

question: Write one way mosquitoes can be controlled without using chemicals.
subject: Science
explanation: Mosquito nets form a physical barrier that stops mosquitoes from biting people at night.
hint: A physical barrier used at night.

question: Name one annual crop which is a cereal.
subject: Science
explanation: Maize is a cereal crop that is planted and harvested within one year.

question: The diagram below shows a method of making water clean. Name the method of making water clean shown above.
subject: Science
explanation: In filtration, dirty water passes through a filter which traps the dirt particles.
hint: Water passes through a clean cloth or filter paper.

question: How does mulching control soil erosion?
subject: Science
answer: Mulches cover the soil and slow down running water
explanation: A mulch cover breaks the force of rain and slows runoff, so soil is not washed away.

question: State one way in which a farmer can promote easy mating in sheep.
subject: Science
answer: By keeping the ram together with the ewes on heat
explanation: Putting the ram with ewes that are on heat makes mating take place easily.
hint: Keep the male and female together.

question: Which type of bee is formed by feeding a grub on royal jelly in its life time?
subject: Science
explanation: A grub fed on royal jelly throughout its life develops into a queen bee.

question: State the importance of using dry wood put on the handle of an iron box.
subject: Science
answer: Dry wood is a poor conductor of heat, so it protects the hand from burns
explanation: The wooden handle does not conduct heat from the hot iron box to the hand.
hint: Wood does not carry heat to the hand.

question: How do insects with mandibles feed?
subject: Science
answer: They bite and chew their food
explanation: Mandibles are strong jaws that bite off and chew food.

question: Which structure enables the trachea to open all the time?
subject: Science
explanation: Rings of cartilage hold the trachea open so that air passes through freely.

question: State any one way the use of biogas conserves trees in the environment.
subject: Science
answer: It reduces the cutting down of trees for firewood
explanation: Families using biogas for cooking no longer cut trees for firewood.

question: The diagram below shows a plant. Identify the plant drawn above.
subject: Science
explanation: The drawing shows a cactus, a plant with a thick fleshy stem and spines instead of leaves.
hint: It has spines instead of leaves.

question: How is the above plant adapted to growing in very dry places?
subject: Science
answer: It has a thick fleshy stem that stores water, and spines that reduce water loss
explanation: The cactus stores water in its stem and its spines lose very little water to the air.
hint: It stores water and loses little of it.

question: Give one way bacteria are useful in septic tanks.
subject: Science
explanation: Bacteria digest the solid waste in septic tanks into harmless liquid.

question: Name the energy change that takes place in a dry cell when the circuit is complete.
subject: Science
explanation: The chemicals inside the dry cell change into electricity when the circuit is complete.
hint: From the chemicals to the current.

question: Why is it not good to induce vomiting when one has taken poisons like paraffin?
subject: Science
answer: Vomiting makes the poison burn the gullet again and it may enter the lungs
explanation: Bringing paraffin up burns the throat a second time and the poison may enter the lungs.

question: How can a dairy farmer identify cows with mastitis infection during milking?
subject: Science
answer: The milk has clots or blood, and the udder is swollen and painful
explanation: Mastitis makes the udder swell and the milk watery with clots.
hint: Look at the milk and the udder.

question: Name one milk breed of goat kept in Uganda.
subject: Science
explanation: Saanen is an exotic dairy goat breed kept in Uganda for milk.

question: Why is it necessary to prepare land before the process of planting crops?
subject: Science
answer: To loosen the soil and remove weeds for proper germination
explanation: Prepared land lets seeds germinate easily and roots grow deep.
hint: Loose, weed-free soil helps seeds grow.

question: How do plants use oxygen gas during germination process?
subject: Science
answer: Oxygen is used in respiration to release energy for germination
explanation: The germinating seed uses oxygen to release energy from stored food so it can grow.

question: Name the body organ that enables human beings to watch a football match on a television.
subject: Science
explanation: We see the match on the television with our eyes.

question: Why are filarial worms dangerous to people?
subject: Science
answer: They cause elephantiasis, which swells body parts
explanation: Filarial worms block the lymph vessels, causing the swelling called elephantiasis.

question: Name the immunisable disease that causes paralysis of the limbs.
subject: Science
explanation: The polio virus attacks the nerves and paralyses the limbs; it is prevented by immunisation.

question: Write down one way in which a magnet is important to a health worker.
subject: Science
answer: It is used to remove small iron pieces from a patient's eye
explanation: A health worker uses a magnet to pull tiny iron splinters out of the eye.
hint: It pulls metal out of the eye.

question: Which method of heat transfer helps us in ironing our clothes?
subject: Science
explanation: Heat moves by conduction from the hot iron box through to the clothes.
hint: Heat travels through the hot metal.

question: Why are children advised to participate in P.E activities?
subject: Science
answer: To keep the body healthy and physically fit
explanation: P.E exercises the body, making children strong and healthy.
hint: For a fit and healthy body.

question: What name is given to a male rabbit?
subject: Science
explanation: A male rabbit is called a buck, while the female is called a doe.
hint: Also the name for a male goat.

question: Mention one way poultry farmers control egg eating in a poultry farm.
subject: Science
explanation: Debeaked birds cannot easily break and eat eggs.

question: In which state of matter is porridge?
subject: Science
explanation: Porridge flows like a liquid, so it is in the liquid state.

question: How does drought lead to lack of food in the environment?
subject: Science
answer: Crops dry up and fail without rain
explanation: Without rain, crops wither and die, so there is no food to harvest.

question: Apart from using pesticides, how else can a farmer control pests in a maize garden?
subject: Science
explanation: Rotating crops breaks the life cycle of pests in the garden.

question: Give one way a short circuit can be prevented in a house.
subject: Science
answer: By using a fuse in the circuit
explanation: A fuse breaks the circuit when too much current flows through it.
hint: A safety device that breaks the circuit.

question: State one way the skeletal system is important to the circulatory system.
subject: Science
explanation: Bones shield the heart, which is the main organ of the circulatory system.

question: How does refrigeration preserve milk?
subject: Science
answer: The cold slows down the growth of germs that sour milk
explanation: Low temperatures make germs inactive, so milk stays fresh for longer.

question: Primary Five pupils of Poyem P/S immersed a stone of mass 500g into water and it displaced 25cm3 of water in the measuring cylinder. Calculate the density of the stone.
subject: Science
explanation: Density = mass / volume = 500 g / 25 cm3 = 20 g/cm3.

question: Give a reason why biceps and triceps are called antagonist muscles.
subject: Science
answer: They work in opposite directions; when one contracts the other relaxes
explanation: The biceps bends the arm while the triceps straightens it, so they oppose each other.

question: 41(b) The following are components of an electric circuit: battery, fuse, switch, bulb. State the use of: (i) a fuse
subject: Science
answer: It breaks the circuit when too much current flows, protecting appliances
explanation: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit before too much current damages appliances.
hint: It is a safety device in the circuit.

question: 41(b) State the use of: (ii) a switch
subject: Science
answer: It opens and closes the circuit (puts the current on and off)
explanation: A switch completes or breaks the path of current in a circuit.
hint: It puts the current on and off.

question: 41(b) State the use of: (iii) battery
subject: Science
answer: It provides the electrical energy that drives current round the circuit
explanation: The battery is the source of electrical energy in the circuit.
hint: It is the source of power.

question: 41(c) State the energy change that takes place in a bulb when a circuit is complete.
subject: Science
answer: Electrical energy to light and heat energy
explanation: The bulb changes electricity into light, and also gives off heat.

question: 42(a) Study the diagram below. Name the family planning method shown above.
subject: Science
explanation: Tubal ligation is a permanent family planning method in which the oviducts are cut and tied.

question: 42(b) How does the above method prevent pregnancies?
subject: Science
answer: The oviducts are cut and tied so eggs cannot meet the sperms
explanation: When the oviducts are blocked, the egg cannot meet sperms and fertilization cannot take place.
hint: The eggs and sperms are kept apart.

question: 42(c) Apart from the above method, give any one other permanent method of family planning.
subject: Science
explanation: Vasectomy is the permanent family planning method for men, in which the sperm ducts are cut and tied.

question: 42(d) State one advantage of family planning.
subject: Science
answer: It enables parents to have only the number of children they can look after
explanation: Family planning lets a family raise the children it can feed, clothe and educate.

question: 43(a) Mention any one crop that can be grown in wetlands.
subject: Science
explanation: Rice grows well in the wet soils of wetlands.

question: 43(b) Apart from growing crops mentioned above, give two other ways people destroy wetlands. (i) ___
subject: Science
explanation: Rubbish dumped in wetlands pollutes the water and kills wetland life.

question: 43(b) Apart from growing crops mentioned above, give two other ways people destroy wetlands. (ii) ___
subject: Science
answer: By digging clay for making bricks
explanation: Digging clay destroys the wetland soil and its plants.

question: 43(c) Write one danger of staying near wetlands.
subject: Science
answer: People are exposed to mosquitoes and water-borne diseases
explanation: Wetlands breed mosquitoes and harbour germs that cause diseases.
hint: Think of mosquitoes and dirty water.

question: 44(a) The diagram below shows changes of states of matter. Name the physical process marked A.
subject: Science
explanation: Sublimation is the change of a solid directly into a gas.

question: 44(a) Name the physical process marked B.
subject: Science
explanation: Melting is the change of a solid into a liquid.

question: 44(b) What happens to the following when water freezes: (i) Volume?
subject: Science
explanation: Water expands when it freezes into ice, so its volume increases.
hint: Ice takes up more space than water.

question: 44(b) What happens to the following when water freezes: (ii) Mass?
subject: Science
explanation: Freezing only changes the state of water, not the amount of matter in it.
hint: No matter is added or lost.

question: 45(a) How is a clinical thermometer important in our daily life?
subject: Science
answer: It measures body temperature to detect fever
explanation: A clinical thermometer shows whether a person has a fever and needs treatment.

question: 45(b) Mention one part of a human body where a clinical thermometer is placed to measure temperature.
subject: Science
explanation: The thermometer is held in the armpit to read body temperature.

question: 45(c) Why can't clinical thermometers be boiled as a way of sterilizing?
subject: Science
answer: The boiling heat would make the mercury expand and break the thermometer
explanation: Boiling would push the mercury beyond the scale and burst the glass tube.

question: 45(c) Give a reason why alcohol is the best liquid to measure the lowest temperature.
subject: Science
answer: Alcohol has a very low freezing point
explanation: Alcohol stays liquid even in extreme cold, so it can measure very low temperatures.

question: 46(a) Study the illustrations below (a new knife, and the same knife after seven months). Name the force that made the knife appear as seen in diagram C.

explanation: A rusted knife loses its sharp edge and cannot cut well.

subject: Science
answer: Grease covers the metal and keeps air and water away from it
explanation: A layer of grease stops air and water from reaching the iron, so rust cannot form.

question: 47(a) State any two types of manure. (i) ___

explanation: Compost manure is made from decayed plant and animal materials.

explanation: Farmyard manure is made from animal droppings and urine.

question: 47(b) State one advantage of using artificial fertilizers over natural fertilizers.
subject: Science
answer: They act faster (are absorbed quickly by crops)
explanation: Artificial fertilizers dissolve quickly so crops get nutrients within a short time.

question: 47(c) Suggest one danger that can result from frequent use of artificial fertilizers.
subject: Science
answer: They can burn the crops and destroy living organisms in the soil
explanation: Too much artificial fertilizer makes the soil acidic and kills useful soil organisms.
hint: Too much of it harms soil and crops.

question: 48. Study the animals below and match correctly. (i) Kangaroo ___
subject: Science
explanation: A kangaroo escapes enemies by hopping away very fast on its strong hind legs.

question: 48(ii) Cat ___
subject: Science
explanation: A cat defends itself and catches prey with its sharp claws.

question: 48(iii) Porcupine ___
subject: Science
explanation: A porcupine protects itself with its sharp spines.

question: 48(iv) Caterpillar ___
subject: Science
explanation: A caterpillar keeps enemies away with its prickly irritating hair.

question: 49(a) Which type of change takes place when a snake moults?

hint: A change in a living thing as it grows.

subject: Science
answer: In a physical change no new substance is formed, while in a chemical change a new substance is formed
explanation: Physical changes only alter appearance, but chemical changes produce new substances.

question: 49(b) Give two differences between physical and chemical changes. (ii) ___
subject: Science
answer: A physical change is reversible while a chemical change is irreversible
explanation: A physical change can be undone, but a chemical change cannot easily be reversed.

question: 49(c) How do snakes benefit from moulting?
subject: Science
answer: It allows the snake to grow (the tight old skin is removed)
explanation: Shedding the old skin gives the growing snake room to increase in size.
hint: It removes the tight old skin.

question: 50(a) The diagram below shows a food chain: Maize plant, Grasshoppers, Birds, Bacteria. Which of the above components acts as: (i) Primary consumer

question: 50(a)(iii) Secondary consumer

explanation: Birds feed on the grasshoppers, so they are secondary consumers.

question: 50(a)(iv) Producer
subject: Science
explanation: The maize plant makes its own food, so it is the producer.

question: 51(a) The diagram below shows an organism under invertebrates. To which group of invertebrates does the above organism belong?

subject: Science
answer: It sucks blood and spreads diseases such as relapsing fever
explanation: Ticks feed on human blood and transmit disease germs.

question: 52(a) The diagram below shows a property of magnets. Identify the property of magnet shown in the diagram above.

answer: Like poles of magnets repel each other
explanation: When two like poles of magnets face each other, they push apart.

question: 52(b) State any two methods of making magnets. (i) ___

question: 52(b) State any two methods of making magnets. (ii) ___
subject: Science
explanation: Passing current through a coil wound round an iron bar makes an electromagnet.

answer: By increasing the number of coils (or increasing the current)
explanation: More turns of wire round the core make the electromagnet stronger.

question: 53(a) Study the intestinal worms below. Identify the worms marked: (i) P

question: 53(c) State any one way of preventing worm marked Q.

answer: By washing hands before eating food
explanation: Washing hands removes roundworm eggs before they enter the mouth.

question: 54(a) List any two examples of scavenger birds. (i) ___

question: 54(a) List any two examples of scavenger birds. (ii) ___

explanation: Vultures feed on the flesh of dead animals.

question: 54(b) How are scavenger birds important in the environment?
subject: Science
answer: They eat dead animals (carrion), keeping the environment clean
explanation: By removing carcasses, scavenger birds stop diseases from spreading.

question: 54(c) Apart from scavenger birds, give any one group of birds.
subject: Science
explanation: Perching birds, like weaver birds, are another group of birds.

question: 55(a) The diagram below shows types of teeth. Name the type of tooth shown: (i) A

explanation: Incisors are the flat front teeth used for cutting food.

question: 55(a)(ii) B

explanation: Canines are the pointed teeth next to the incisors, used for tearing food.

question: 55(b) Give the use of the above type of teeth in man. (i) A
subject: Science
explanation: Incisors have sharp edges that cut food into pieces.

question: 55(b)(ii) B
subject: Science
explanation: Canines are pointed so they tear tough food like meat.

question: Name any one example of a flowering plant.
subject: Science
explanation: Maize is a flowering plant because it produces flowers that develop into grains.

question: Which component of air supports burning?
subject: Science
explanation: Oxygen in the air supports burning; things cannot burn without it.

question: State any one use of water in promoting personal hygiene.
subject: Science
explanation: Bathing with clean water keeps the body clean and healthy.

question: Give the type of poultry reared for egg production.
subject: Science
explanation: Layers are chickens kept specially for laying eggs.

question: Which element of weather helps in winnowing harvested crops?

explanation: Wind blows away the light chaff from the heavier grains during winnowing.

question: Apart from the above crop, mention any one other example of a root crop.

explanation: Sweet potatoes are root crops whose swollen roots store food.

question: Why does a drone bee die after mating a queen bee?

hint: Part of its body breaks off.

question: What type of immunity is acquired through taking breast milk?
subject: Science
explanation: The baby receives ready-made antibodies from the mother's milk without making them itself.

question: State the best method of making water safe for drinking.

hint: Heat the water until it bubbles.

question: How is a dustbin useful in a classroom?
subject: Science
answer: It keeps rubbish, helping to keep the classroom clean
explanation: A dustbin collects waste papers and dirt so the classroom stays clean.

question: Which garden tool is used for light weeding?

explanation: A hand fork is used to dig out small weeds near crops.

question: State any one characteristic of a housefly which makes it an insect.
subject: Science
explanation: All insects, including the housefly, have six legs.

question: Give any one way of controlling mosquitoes at home.
subject: Science
answer: By draining stagnant water around the home
explanation: Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water, so draining it stops them from multiplying.

question: Why are canine teeth able to tear meat?
subject: Science
explanation: The sharp pointed shape of canines lets them pierce and tear meat.

question: The diagram below shows a head of a tapeworm. Name the part marked K.
subject: Science
explanation: The head (scolex) of a tapeworm has hooks that grip the wall of the intestines.

question: How does the above intestinal worm enter our body?
subject: Science
explanation: Tapeworm larvae in half-cooked pork or beef grow into worms in our intestines.

question: State any one use of honey in industries.
subject: Science
answer: It is used for making sweets
explanation: Factories use honey as a sweetener in sweets and cough syrups.
hint: A sweet product made from it.

question: Which disease vector spreads relapsing fever to people?
subject: Science
explanation: Ticks bite people and pass on the germs that cause relapsing fever.

question: How is a moth able to pollinate flowers at night?
subject: Science
answer: It visits flowers guided by their scent
explanation: Night flowers produce a strong scent that attracts moths to pollinate them.

question: State any one reason why animals move from one place to another.
subject: Science
explanation: Animals move to places where they can find enough food to eat.
hint: In search of something to eat.

question: State the difference between a vector and a germ.

answer: A vector carries and transmits germs, while a germ causes the disease
explanation: Vectors like mosquitoes spread germs, but it is the germ that makes a person sick.

question: Give any one way in which food is important to the human body.
subject: Science
explanation: Food provides energy that the body uses to work and play.

question: Why do some objects sink in water?

question: The diagram below shows a maize grain. Name the part marked Y.

hint: The food store of the seed.

question: Why is rain regarded as the main natural source of water on earth?

answer: All other natural sources like rivers, wells and springs are fed by rain
explanation: Rain fills rivers, lakes and underground water, so it is the mother of all water sources.

question: How is a safety pin useful when giving first aid to casualties?
subject: Science
answer: It fastens bandages and slings in place
explanation: A safety pin holds bandages firmly so they do not fall off the wound.

question: State any one importance of the spur to a cock.
subject: Science
answer: It uses it for fighting and protection
explanation: A cock fights enemies and rivals using its sharp spurs.

question: Name any one vaccine given to babies at birth.

question: Apart from a leaf, name any one other object that floats on water.
subject: Science
explanation: Dry wood is less dense than water, so it floats.

question: Which rabbit disease causes wounds in their ears?

explanation: Ear canker is a rabbit disease that causes sores and wounds in the ears.

question: State any one reason why a passion fruit plant climbs a mango plant.

explanation: Earthworms breathe through their moist skin; oil blocks it and suffocates them.

question: State any one condition which makes bees swarm.

question: Why are plants not able to make their own food at night?

question: The diagram below shows a body structure. Name the body structure shown in the diagram above.

question: Which group of insects do not live, move and work together?

question: Name the weather instrument used to measure the amount of rainfall received in an area.
subject: Science
explanation: A rain gauge collects and measures the rain that falls in an area.

question: 41(a) Name any two items found in a First Aid box. (i) ___
subject: Science
explanation: A bandage is used to cover and protect wounds.

question: 41(a) Name any two items found in a First Aid box. (ii) ___
subject: Science
explanation: A plaster covers small cuts to keep out dirt and germs.

question: 41(b) Give any two reasons why a casualty is given First Aid. (i) ___
subject: Science
explanation: Quick first aid can keep a casualty alive before the doctor arrives.

question: 41(b) Give any two reasons why a casualty is given First Aid. (ii) ___
subject: Science
answer: To prevent the condition from becoming worse
explanation: First aid stops bleeding and pain from increasing before proper treatment.

question: 42(a) The diagram below shows a flower. Name the parts marked T and U. (i) T

question: 42(b) Why is part marked V brightly coloured in some flowers?

question: 42(c) What does part marked W develop into after fertilization?

explanation: After fertilization the ovary swells and develops into a fruit.

question: 43(a) Name two solutes used to prepare Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS). (i) ___

question: 43(a) Name two solutes used to prepare Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS). (ii) ___

explanation: Sugar gives the body energy in the ORS mixture.

question: 43(b) Why should a person preparing Oral Rehydration Solution wash his/her hands first?
